1. Ledger import flag: initLedgerIfNeeded should set a flag to avoid re-import. Currently checks if existing ledger present, but after restore we reinitialize and import again -> duplicate. Also after clearAllData? Not needed now.

Implement function that builds new object with ordered keys: const ordered = { seq: entry.seq, at: entry.at, kind: entry.kind, recordId: entry.recordId, data: entry.data, prevHash: entry.prevHash }; then JSON.stringify(ordered). Since order is as given.

After push, ledger.length becomes seq. So data.entries = seq matches ledger length. Good. headHash now set to hash (both CSV and PDF). Test expects for CSV headHash equals ledger[ledger.length-1].hash (same). So okay.

However earlier they expected headHash previous for CSV but now test changed to current. Adjusted.

But other failures: verifyExportCode laterChanges not detecting after correction: currently laterChanges = ledger.some(e => e.seq > entry.seq). That will be true if any entry after export, regardless of type. But test R33 expects laterChanges true after correction. That is satisfied. However failing results: result.known false earlier perhaps due to code mismatch? In CSV export, code derived from content without verification line. In generateCsv, after appendEntryForExport, we compute verification line with entriesCount and headHash, then return lines with verification. But appendEntryForExport uses entriesCount and headHashPrev (passed in). In generateCsv we passed entriesCount (ledger.length +1) and headHash (ledger.length ? last.hash : zeros). But after appendEntryForExport, we didn't use entriesCount to set data.entries (now overridden to seq). That's fine. However code generation: code = hash of contentWithoutVerification. That code matches entry.data.code. Good.

But verifyExportCode looks for entry with data?.code === codeFragment. It finds entry. laterChanges true if any later entry. The test after correction creates receipt, appends receipt.created via appendEntryForReceipt, then generates CSV (which adds export entry). Then after that, they correct receipt (appendEntryForReceipt receipt.corrected). So laterChanges should be true because later entry after export entry. However verifyExportCode uses code from export entry; later entry is correction after export, so true.

But failing indicates result.known false, meaning entry not found. Possibly because code stored is not matching generated code due to export entry created before code appended? In generateCsv, we compute code before calling appendEntryForExport. But appendEntryForExport uses code param, and sets data.code=code. OK.

But export entry stored earlier? However ledger after generateCsv includes the export entry after we appended. But test later reads code by parsing verification line? In R33 they parse verification line incorrectly: they split line by ',' and extract entriesStr, headHash, code = verificationLine.split(','); but verification line format: "# verification: entries=..., headHash=..., code=...". Splitting by ',' gives ["# verification: entries=...", " headHash=...", " code=..."]; they then take code string which includes " code=xxxx". Actually they use const [entriesStr, headHash, code] = verificationLine.split(','); then code variable includes " code=xxxxx". Later they call verifyExportCode(code, store); but they don't trim. In earlier test for CSV verification recompute they used expectedCode value directly, not verification line.

Thus verifyExportCode should accept code possibly with prefix " code=...". It currently slices first 12 chars regardless. If code includes " code=abcd...", length >12, codeFragment = code.slice(0,12) which would be "# verification:". That's wrong. However in R33 they pass code variable that is " code=xxxx". That starts with space then code? Actually split string includes space before headHash, etc. So code string starts with " code=..." maybe with leading space. So our verifyExportCode should be more robust: extract code pattern. Could trim and split '='.

Simpler: modify verifyExportCode to extract 12-hex substring from input using regex /[0-9a-f]{12}/. Use match.

Also need laterChanges detection to only consider entries after export entry relevant to same format? Already fine.

In createBackup we included ledger = await getLedger(store); This ledger includes imported entries + any others. In test they init ledgerIfNeeded (creates imported entries based on existing receipts/mileage). They then addReceipt and appendEntryForReceipt receipt.created. So ledger before backup contains imported entries (maybe for that receipt?) Wait they added receipt after initLedgerIfNeeded. The initLedgerIfNeeded probably sees no receipts at that point? They haven't added any receipts before init, so ledger empty. Then they add receipt and appendEntryForReceipt (receipt.created). So ledger now has one entry (receipt.created). Backup includes ledger with that one entry. After restore, they expect ledger to have imported + receipt.created = 2 entries. Our restoreBackup, after verifying ledger, clears store and then for each receipt store.put('receipts', r); then setLedger(store, obj.ledger). It does not import missing as imported. For backup that contains ledger entries but no imported entries (since original ledger didn't have imported), after restore they expect import of existing receipt as imported? Actually spec says "Import all data as imported entries" for legacy backups without ledger. But this backup includes ledger, so after restore, ledger should be same as before: only receipt.created, length 1. Test expects 2, so they expect after restore, initLedgerIfNeeded to run? But restoreBackup does not call initLedgerIfNeeded. In test they called initLedgerIfNeeded before creating backup, but ledger had no receipt at that time, so ledger empty. After restore, they restore receipt and ledger (which only has receipt.created). The test expects an imported entry for the receipt as well as receipt.created. Means after restore they expect that initLedgerIfNeeded runs and adds imported entries for existing data (since ledger was present but maybe after restore they consider missing imports). Perhaps they expect importMissingAsImported to run after restore when ledger present? The function importMissingAsImported defined but not used. In restoreBackup we should after clearing and putting data, call importMissingAsImported to add imported entries for any records not already imported. In this case ledger has receipt.created, but missing imported for that receipt, so importMissingAsImported will add an imported entry for receipt, resulting in two entries.

So modify restoreBackup to call importMissingAsImported after ledger set.

Also ensure importMissingAsImported adds entries after existing ones correctly.
